newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's health sector needs credits for drugs.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's health sector needs credits for drugs.

text.p: Serbia's health sector is in a poor financial situation due to unpaid social security contributions and the monopolistic behaviour of drug producers, Belgrade newspapers reported on Friday.

"Companies are unable to pay even the reduced social security benefits of 14 percent (on wages), which has stemmed the inflow of funds and is jeopardising even the minimum health protection," Serbian Health Minister Leposava Milicevic was quoted by the daily Politika as saying.

She said domestic drug producers declined to extend credits to the health sector for a period longer than 180 days, which was the only way it saw to obtaining necessary drugs and other sanitary materials.
Milicevic urged domestic medicine producers to agree to long-term credit arrangements and said that if they weren't ready to do so, foreign firms were.
She said there were offers from Swiss, Swedish and Austrian pharmaceutical companies to supply drugs on one-year or longer-term credits, but did not specify.
The only domestic producers to extend medicines on loan were Velefarm and ICN (Galenika) Yugoslavia, a subsidiary of California-based ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc.
ICN (Galenika) has supplied medicaments to the value of $50 million and Velefarm $10 million and will pay their social security benefits also in drugs.
Despite rigorous control of health fund contributions there is a 270 million dinar ($55.7 million) shortage in the fund's coffers.

"The fact that 90 percent of the collected funds are used for wages shows how little remains for other needs," Milicevic said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305 ($ = 4.85 Yugoslav Dinars)
